hits.title: TWO PROKOFIEVS, PETER, A WOLF, AND A DJ
hits.content:
Your wcfsymphony brings together the music of two Prokofievs — Sergei and his grandson Gabriel — in an unforgettable blend of classical tradition, modern innovation, and storytelling.
The concert begins with Sergei Prokofiev’s spirited Classical Symphony, a witty and energetic work inspired by the music of Haydn and Mozart. Then, classical music meets the turntable with Gabriel Prokofiev’s groundbreaking Concerto for Turntables and Orchestra, featuring award-winning Chicago turntablist DJ RTST (pronounced “Artist”).
The evening concludes with one of classical music’s most beloved musical adventures, Sergei Prokofiev’s Peter and the Wolf, featuring beloved longtime KWWL anchorman Ron Steele as guest narrator.
Two Prokofievs. A DJ. A wolf. And an Iowa broadcasting legend. This is one concert you won’t want to miss!

hits.title: Woven Conference 2026
hits.content:
Woven 2026 is a one-day gathering that takes the intersection of faith and mental health seriously. Led by best-selling author and therapist Aundi Kolber and featuring Kayla Craig, Kelsey Kramer McGinnis, Stuart Hall, and more, our hope is to have honest conversations about spiritual, mental, and emotional health and create a space where you can finally exhale.
This year we'll explore what it looks like to stay curious, stay kind to yourself, and hold onto your faith even as it evolves.
Tickets are $25 and include:
- Breakfast, lunch, and snacks
- Full access to all sessions and workshops
- A free book of your choice by one of the speakers

hits.title: Cedar Valley Plant-Based Holiday Market
hits.content:
Join us for a cozy holiday experience with vegan vendors, seasonal treats, handmade gifts, festive workshops, creative activities, and a welcoming sense of community.
Whether you've been plant-based for years or are simply curious about exploring more vegan-friendly options, this event is designed to be warm, approachable, and enjoyable for everyone.
Browse local and regional vendors offering plant-based foods, gifts, art, candles, self-care products, home goods, holiday items, and more. Throughout the day, enjoy workshops and seasonal experiences.
The Cedar Valley Plant-Based Holiday Market is more than just shopping. It's about creating a meaningful seasonal tradition centered around kindness, creativity, and community.
We want this event to feel cozy, welcoming, and memorable for families, friends, longtime vegans, vegetarians, plant-curious guests, and anyone looking for a different kind of holiday experience in the Cedar Valley.
Come celebrate the season with festive food, creative experiences, local vendors, and plant-based holiday magic in the heart of the Midwest.

hits.title: Illuminate the Garden at the Cedar Valley Arboretum
hits.content:
Illuminate the Gardens at Cedar Valley Arboretum & Botanic Gardens
Experience the magic of the holiday season at Illuminate the Gardens, a festive outdoor light experience at the Cedar Valley Arboretum & Botanic Gardens in Waterloo, Iowa! Stroll through beautiful garden landscapes transformed by twinkling lights and seasonal displays as the Arboretum becomes a sparkling winter wonderland. Whether you're planning a family outing, a date night, or a holiday tradition with friends, Illuminate the Gardens offers a memorable way to celebrate the season surrounded by nature.
Bundle up and enjoy the beauty of the illuminated gardens, gather around the cozy bonfire, roast marshmallows, and warm up with a cup of hot chocolate. With a welcoming atmosphere and opportunities to slow down and enjoy the outdoors, this seasonal event invites visitors of all ages to make special holiday memories.
Illuminate the Gardens runs November 27 through December 26, 2026, on Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 5:30–9:30 p.m. Make Illuminate the Gardens part of your holiday plans and discover the beauty of nature in a whole new light! The Cedar Valley Arboretum & Botanic Gardens is located at 1927 East Orange Road, Waterloo, Iowa. For more information, visit cedarvalleyarboretum.org.

hits.title: Friendsgiving: Mashed Potatoes and Murder-Mystery Dinner
hits.content:
“Every year, the same group of frenemies gathers for their ‘Friendsgiving Feast.’ But this year, the gravy isn’t the only thing thick with tension. As the drinks flow and the turkey cools, old betrayals bubble up with the cranberry sauce. And when one guest turns up very dead half-
way through dinner, the rest must carve through the gossip, the grudges, and the gluten-free stuffing to find the killer among their closest friends.”
“The only thing colder than the leftovers... is the body.”
Original interactive mystery where you play a role. You may be the victim or the perpetrator.
Event takes approximately 3 hours, is held in a historic home with stairs required to enter, overnight stay not required- but can be added.
Friday, November 27th: 6pm Friendsgiving Murder Mystery Dinner- Salad, Meatloaf or Vegetarian Lasagna, Roasted baby potatoes, candied baby carrots, and assorted Cheesecakes. Tickets are $75 each or 2 for $120 + tax (must select the 2 ticket option for discount)

hits.title: Museum Store Sunday 2026
hits.content:
The Museum will be open from 10:00 AM-2:00 PM Sunday, November 29th for our annual Museum Store Sunday event!
This year we will have amazing deals in the store, and for the first time, the Museum will also be open for regular admission. Shopping in the store is free.
On the Sunday following Thanksgiving, over 2,200 museum stores representing all fifty states and the District of Columbia, twenty-five countries, and five continents will offer inspired shopping at your favorite museums and cultural institutions. Museum Store Sunday offers a special shopping experience in one-of-a-kind stores, showcasing broad assortments of highly curated, unique, mission-related gifts. From books to jewelry to home accessories, stationery and children’s products, there is always something for everyone. Shop knowing you are supporting the missions and programs of each participating museum and cultural institution.

hits.title: Imaginarium Science Gallery Grand Opening
hits.content:
The Grout Museum District’s new Imaginarium Science Gallery will open to the public on Tuesday, December 15, 2026 with extended hours, 10AM-7PM, bringing hands-on science exploration and discovery back to the Cedar Valley in a new space inside the Grout Museum of History and Science.
The new gallery marks an exciting next chapter for the children’s science center, which inspired curiosity and learning for 32 years at its former Washington Street location. The move into the main Grout Museum building allows the District to continue offering engaging science experiences for children and families in a refreshed, more accessible space designed for future generations.
Visitors can look forward to a variety of interactive exhibits that encourage experimentation, problem-solving, creativity and play. From brand new exhibits that send objects through twisting pathways in A-Mazing Airways to exploring motion with Pendulum Waves and a physics Roller Coaster, the gallery will offer opportunities to discover scientific concepts through hands-on experiences. Other new exhibits, as well as old favorites that visitors may remember from the Imaginarium building, will invite visitors to explore light, color, patterns, air pressure, static electricity and more.
The Imaginarium Science Gallery brings together new exhibits and returning favorites, honoring the legacy of Carl and Peggy Bluedorn while creating new opportunities for children and families to learn through play.
“We are excited to welcome visitors into this new space and continue the Imaginarium’s tradition of inspiring curiosity,” said Margaret Moye, Executive Director of the Grout Museum District. “This project allows us to build on what generations of families have loved about the Imaginarium while creating new opportunities for exploration and discovery.”
The gallery is made possible through the District’s Reimagine the Imag: Inspiring Curiosity for Future Generations campaign, which supports the renovation, new exhibits and long-term sustainability of the science space.
Additional details about the opening will be announced closer to the opening date.

hits.title: Battle of Waterloo
hits.content: Welcome to Iowa’s premier high school wrestling tournament – the Battle of Waterloo!In its second decade, the Battle of Waterloo has earned a reputation as an exciting, well-run three-day tournament featuring wrestling teams from every corner of the state. The matches never disappoint as some of the state’s most elite wrestlers square off in a 24-team girls bracket and a 32-team boys bracket.

hits.title: Museum School Grandparents Night-Fall Semester
hits.content: Join us for Museum School Grandparents Night, a special evening open house-style where students become the guides and teachers! Grandparents, parents and museum school alumni are invited to explore the museum alongside their grandchildren or children, enjoy student-led tours, and take part in hands-on activities inspired by our Museum School lessons – from science experiments to pioneer-era challenges. This celebration show cases everything students have learned throughout the year while creating meaningful shared memories.

hits.title: Voices of Iowa: Korean War Documentary Premiere
hits.content:
Experience the untold stories of courage, sacrifice, and survival through the eyes of Iowa veterans in the premiere of Voices of Iowa: Korean War. The powerful next installment in our Voices of Iowa documentary series brings their firsthand accounts to life. Through intimate interviews, rare archival footage, and cinematic reenactments, discover the deeply personal stories of those who served in a war too often forgotten. Cost: $5, Museum Members Free
Location: Waterloo Center for the Arts
Content Advisory: This documentary contains depictions of combat violence and firsthand accounts of traumatic experiences that may be disturbing to some viewers.
Rated PG13

hits.title: Family Friendly Open Game Nights
hits.content:
Join Dark Vassal Gaming and the Friendly Meeples at the Sullivan Brothers Iowa Veterans Museum for a monthly family friendly game night!
Date: 1st Thursday of the Month
Time: 5:00-9:00 p.m.
Location: Mess Hall and Lobby at the Sullivan Brothers Iowa Veterans Museum (under the Mustang P-51 plane)
Free admission, but donations appreciated. Concessions and cash bar available for purchase with proceeds supporting the Grout Museum District's Sullivan Brothers Iowa Veteran Museum.
Available Games: Risk, Iowaopoly, Bingo, Minecraft Builders and Biomes, Scrabble, Warhammer and more!
Guests are also welcome to bring their own games to share!

hits.title: Storytime Under the Stars 26-27
hits.content:
Storytime Under the Stars takes place on the first Saturday of the month. Enjoy a cozy story time just for toddlers in our planetarium. Snuggle up in your pajamas and bring your favorite stuffed animal! Listen to several delightful tales read by a museum educator beneath a sky full of twinkling stars.
Doors open at 9:30AM. Stories begin at 10AM. Cost is $3 per person.
